title: Pea and Mint Soup
subtitle: Bright spring soup with frozen peas and fresh mint
excerpt: Frozen peas barely cooked in hot vegetable stock and blended with shallots, garlic, and fresh mint into a vivid green soup. Ready in 15 minutes. Served chilled in summer or hot from the pot in spring.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pea and mint soup is one of the quickest soups in the British canon, relying on frozen peas which are available year-round and provide a brighter, sweeter flavour than fresh podded peas out of season. The secret is speed: the peas must be barely cooked to preserve their colour and sweetness. Overcooked peas turn from bright green to khaki. Blend immediately and serve.

recipeTools.notes: Or a stand blender for a finer texture.

content.text: Speed is everything: the peas go in frozen and are blended the moment they are just tender. Every extra minute on the heat dulls the colour. Add the mint leaves after blending: cooking them destroys the fresh flavour. Serve immediately, or cool rapidly in iced water and refrigerate if serving chilled.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the hot stock and bring to a simmer. Add the frozen peas. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the peas are just tender and bright green. Do not overcook.
Remove from the heat. Add the mint leaves. Blend immediately until very smooth. Add the lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately for a hot soup. For a chilled summer version, transfer to a bowl set over iced water, stir to cool quickly, then refrigerate for up to 2 hours. Serve in chilled bowls.
